policy_title: Reform media ownership and support local news
stated: Tighten rules on media ownership so no individual or company owns more than 20% of a media market. Implement the 2012 Leveson Report recommendations and reinstate the second part of the review. Support local media with new grants.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for rules on media to be tightened so that no individual or company owns more than 20% of a media market. We would implement the recommendations of the 2012 Leveson Report and reinstate the second part of that crucial review to ensure the UK media are held to the highest ethical standards. We will support local media through new grants to encourage the growth of a wider range of civic-minded local news publishers.

bearing_set.reason: Capping media ownership at 20%, implementing Leveson press regulation recommendations, and reinstating the inquiry directly bear on free expression (plurality of voices), privacy (Leveson was triggered by phone-hacking/privacy violations), democratic rights (concentration of media power over informed voting), and press accountability/due process — all within O9's strict scope.

Media ownership caps and Leveson-style press regulation directly constrain freedom of expression, property rights, and editorial autonomy — concrete mechanisms that move the personal liberty and free speech indicators, in the 'worsens' direction from a press-freedom standpoint.
Grants for local news directly sustain the civic-information infrastructure underpinning social trust, civic participation and community belonging — the core O15 indicators.

membership_note: Three distinct mechanisms: a liberty/press-freedom cost (O10), a democratic-plurality and rule-of-law benefit (O9), and a community-cohesion benefit via local media (O15). Fiscal cost of grants is unspecified and likely small-scale — insufficient to clear the non-negligible bar for O12.
